text:
vikram: Heads-up: seeing large tail latency in otel-collector when exporting to Splunk HEC during ingestion spikes. Spans/logs queue up, memory_limiter trips, and we end up with 20–30s stalls. Anyone else notice this?

marta: yep saw it around 03:12 UTC yesterday. Splunk endpoint was slow, queued_retry kept retrying and the collector kept growing mem usage. CPU spiked too.

leo: Tempo and Jaeger were fine for traces when I checked, so feels exporter-specific.

vikram: confirmed — Tempo/Jaeger look healthy. Problem seems to be fanout: we send traces to tempo + jaeger + honeycomb and also forward logs to Splunk. That multiplies payloads and makes Splunk the bottleneck.

jamie: we currently use a single traces pipeline with queued_retry + batch + memory_limiter. queued_retry is global so one slow exporter backpressure affects everything. We should consider per-exporter queues or separate pipelines per vendor.

marta: agreed. quick config sketch: split traces pipeline into `traces/tempo` and `traces/splunk` so each can have its own `queued_retry` and `batch` config. Also tune `memory_limiter` lower for the splunk pipeline.

leo: can we also add per-tenant sampling before fanout? A heavy tenant causes 3x amplification today. tail_sampling or attribute-based sampling could cut load.

jamie: yes — either (a) ingress sampling per-tenant (recommended) or (b) tail_sampling with a shorter lookback for high-volume tenants. We should avoid global head-based drop since it affects accuracy for low-traffic tenants.

vikram: rough `otelcol` snippet for per-exporter pipeline idea:

```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}

processors:
  memory_limiter:
    limit_mib: 1024
    spike_limit_mib: 256
  batch: {}
  queued_retry/tempo: {}
  queued_retry/splunk: {}

exporters:
  tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.redwood.internal:14268
  splunk_hec:
    token: "***"
    endpoint: https://splunk-ingest.company:8088

service:
  pipelines:
    traces/tempo:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch, queued_retry/tempo]
      exporters: [tempo]

    traces/splunk:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch, queued_retry/splunk]
      exporters: [splunk_hec]
```

marta: also add `max_concurrent_requests` / circuit-breaker at the exporter client if possible. Splunk HEC supports rate-limiting responses; we should honor `retry_after` and back off more aggressively.

leo: what about retention/cost controls? If we can route lower-signal spans to a cheaper long-term store (S3 + query index) and only keep high-signal spans in Tempo/Honeycomb, that'd help unit cost.

vikram: good call. propose: low-priority spans -> object-storage sink + small index for debug, high-priority -> tempo/jaeger/honeycomb. Priority can be based on `tenant`, `service.name`, and sampling score.

jamie: short-term ops plan: 1) create separate splunk pipeline in staging with tighter memory_limiter and per-exporter queued_retry, 2) route 10% of traffic from prod to that staging pipeline via header-based routing for canary, 3) enable per-tenant head-based sampling for top 5 noisy tenants, 4) add exporter-level circuit-breaker metrics to console dashboards.

marta: I'll file the issue and own the staging config canary.

vikram: thanks — @marta you're owner. Can we target a small rollout tonight PST?

marta: yes, I'll push a config PR in ~30m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config PR 4623 merged to telemetry/staging; rollout to staging started (otel-collector-telemetry-staging-1).

ops-bot: ops-bot: alert: splunk_hec_5xx_rate increased from 0.2% to 4.7% between 02:57 and 03:15 UTC.

leo: nice — staging rollout will let us validate backpressure isolation. If stable, we can do 10% prod traffic via header split in envoy next week.

jamie: follow-ups: add console panels for `exporter_queued_length{exporter=\"splunk_hec\"}`, `exporter_retry_count`, and `collector_memory_bytes`. Also add alert when queued length > 10k for >1m.

vikram: thanks team. quick wins: split pipelines, per-exporter queued_retry, per-tenant sampling for biggest offenders.

marta: :thumbsup: I'll update the ticket with test plan and rollback criteria.

leo: :eyes: ping me when the canary is up, I'll watch latency percentiles in Tempo/Jaeger as well.

vikram: added to the rollout doc.

marta: closing loop — PR up, config applied in staging, will monitor for 30m then propose prod header split.
